subsystems.name: Qubit encoding
subsystems.role: turns the chemistry problem into qubits, one orbital per qubit (or fewer with symmetries).

subsystems.name: Hamiltonian
subsystems.role: expresses the molecule's energy as a weighted sum of measurable Pauli terms.
parts: one- and two-electron integrals from a classical chemistry package

subsystems.name: Ansatz circuit
subsystems.role: a shallow parameterised circuit that prepares a trial wavefunction.
parts: problem-inspired form (e.g. UCCSD) or hardware-efficient form

subsystems.name: Measurement and expectation estimation
subsystems.role: estimates the energy of each Pauli term by repeated circuit execution.

subsystems.name: Classical optimiser
subsystems.role: updates the circuit parameters to lower the measured energy.

subsystems.name: Quantum processor and control
subsystems.role: executes the circuit many times per iteration.

buildSteps.title: Pick the target and trim the problem
buildSteps.detail: Choose a molecule and the orbitals that matter chemically. Freeze core orbitals and discard high-energy virtual ones so the active space fits the available qubits — a 12-qubit calculation is already a squeeze on today's hardware.

buildSteps.title: Compute the integrals classically
buildSteps.detail: A classical chemistry program calculates the one- and two-electron integrals in a chosen basis set (for example STO-3G), giving the numerical coefficients of the electronic Hamiltonian.

buildSteps.title: Map fermions onto qubits
buildSteps.detail: Apply a fermion-to-qubit transform so each spin-orbital becomes a qubit. This expands a handful of terms into hundreds or thousands of Pauli strings, which is where measurement cost is decided.

buildSteps.title: Design the ansatz
buildSteps.detail: Choose a circuit family and depth. It must be expressive enough to approach the true ground state, shallow enough to survive noise, and structured to avoid barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially.

buildSteps.title: Measure the terms on hardware
buildSteps.detail: Group commuting Pauli strings so one circuit setting measures many terms, then run thousands of shots per setting. Error mitigation (readout correction, zero-noise extrapolation) nudges the expectation values back toward the noiseless answer.

buildSteps.title: Close the classical loop
buildSteps.detail: Feed the estimated energy to a classical optimiser, which proposes new parameters. Repeat until the energy stops falling — typically hundreds to thousands of hardware executions per run.

buildSteps.title: Validate against a classical answer
buildSteps.detail: Compare with exact diagonalisation or coupled-cluster results for the same active space. Chemical accuracy means about 1 kcal/mol (4.2 kJ/mol), or roughly 1.6 mHa; without this check a converged number proves nothing.

buildSteps.title: Scale or reach for fault tolerance
buildSteps.detail: For molecules of industrial interest, deepen the circuit, add symmetry reduction and improve ansätze; ultimately move to error-corrected logical qubits, where phase estimation may replace the variational loop entirely.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum processors with tens to hundreds of physical qubits
prerequisites.why: circuits can be run today, but coherence and connectivity still cap the achievable depth.
each layer of gates adds error, so ansatz depth is limited to shallow circuits that may miss the true ground state.
estimating thousands of Pauli terms to useful precision is expensive; grouping and mitigation reduce but do not remove the cost.
logical qubits below the error threshold were reported in 2024, but nowhere near the scale needed for a useful chemistry problem.
methods such as exact diagonalisation and coupled cluster set the accuracy bar — and often already match what variational algorithms deliver.

pathway.milestone: ground-state energies of small molecules (hydrogen, lithium hydride, and similar) computed on 4–20 qubit devices
pathway.unlocks: a working experimental pipeline and honest benchmarks against classical chemistry.

pathway.milestone: error mitigation plus smarter ansätze push active-space calculations toward roughly 50–100 qubits
pathway.unlocks: small transition-metal and catalyst fragments where classical methods strain.

pathway.milestone: hybrid workflows that split a problem between a classical supercomputer and a quantum processor
pathway.unlocks: embedding quantum subroutines in real chemistry pipelines rather than isolated demos.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant execution of chemistry circuits, likely with phase estimation rather than a variational loop
pathway.unlocks: energies and reaction barriers beyond classical reach, if a genuine advantage is ever demonstrated.
